name: MA-06
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The district's D+11 lean, Koh's roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays elevated, but nothing suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Koh, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Massachusetts' 6th District is an open seat after Seth Moulton left to run for Senate, but it remains firmly Democratic territory with an 11-point partisan lean. Dan Koh has built a dominant financial position, raising about $4.7 million with $2 million on hand and outside support, while Republican Micah Jones has raised under $450,000 with minimal cash remaining.

Prediction markets give the Democratic candidate roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no outside groups are spending against Koh. With no public polling available, the forecast leans on fundamentals, which all favor Democrats by a wide margin. The main source of uncertainty is the lack of polling data in an open-seat race, but the structural advantages make an upset unlikely.
